name: Subagent Model Router
description: Give Cindy's subagents a model chain: pick models per group in a settings page, drag to order them, and the next model takes over when one fails. Ships its own Pi extension and installs or removes it in one click.
whenToUse: When subagents should run on cheaper models, when a model keeps failing and the next one should take over, or when providers and models need grouping for different task difficulty.

items.name: guide
items.description: How Subagent Router maps groups to a fallback chain and installs its Pi extension

tools.name: router_status
tools.description: Report whether the Pi extension is injected, where its files live, the saved model groups, and the default group. Read-only.

tools.name: router_install
tools.description: Write the bundled Pi extension to the stable extension directory and register it in Cindy's Pi extension settings. Idempotent: repeating it changes nothing. Takes effect in the next new task.

tools.name: router_uninstall
tools.description: Remove the Pi extension entry and delete its files, leaving no residue. Idempotent: repeating it reports nothing to do.

tools.name: router_config_get
tools.description: Return the saved model groups, their descriptions and their model order. Read-only.

tools.name: router_config_set
tools.description: Replace the whole group configuration. Each group has id, name, description and an ordered models list of {id, provider, name}; defaultGroupId picks the chain used by default.

config.description: Full configuration object: { enabled, defaultGroupId, groups: [{ id, name, description, models: [{ id, provider, name }] }] }
